scenario: [LFST.9.3.6]: a replayer pairs each recorded `timetag` with the re-derived one the first time either occurs, and every later atom "must agree with that pairing in both directions: a recorded `timetag` met with a second re-derived one, or a re-derived `timetag` met with a second recorded one, is the Divergence". This vector holds the second direction. One Trig assert and a pump fire `r` once, and its RHS calls `svc.put`. So the firing's begin RuleFireAnnotation and its CallIssued carry one `timetag`. The harness ([RCTS.1.2.18]) gives the CallIssued, call 0, a `timetag` no atom in the recording carries (`split_timetag`), so the firing's atoms carry two recorded `timetag`s. On replay the begin annotation pairs the recorded `timetag` with the re-derived one; the CallIssued then re-derives that same `timetag` against a second recorded one, and the replay must stop with DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE (-725). The unaltered recording must replay, so the refusal is the split's. What it discriminates: a replayer that keeps only a recorded-to-re-derived map meets a recorded `timetag` it has not seen, pairs it and goes on, so it replays the altered recording without refusal. `LFST.9.3.6_timetag_pairing_broken_diverges` (`merge_timetags`) holds the first direction, which that one-way map does catch. NOT PINNED: the Divergence's `seq`, which `replay_refused` does not read. PATHS: libds's `Engine.replay` in verify mode, its two-way pairing in `rfcs/codec.c` (unit case `tt_split_call` in test_rfcs_verify.c); the Mercury runtime's `ds.replay` pairing (`lfst_9_3_6_pair`, unit check `check_replay_timetag_call`), which ends the replay `diverged`.
